body:
I have been struggling with opioid dependency for the past eight years or so.  I have been in and out of prison due largely to the drug Heroin.  For the past year and a half, Methadone has been a part of my daily life.  Methadone clinics offer an escape for people like me, who spend all of their time using and seeking a Heroin fix.  I go in once a day, sign in a client number and have a seat.  Once my number is called, I go to the 'dosing room' where I sign a daily log, and recieve my orange Methadone tablets (slighty moistened to discourage clients from pocketing the tablets) in a paper cup.  I pour some more water, stir the tabs, drink and go.  And for the duration of 24-36 hours, the thought of 'using' is nowhere in mind.  The first day I got on the Methadone Maintance program, I was in bad shape.  Tired of spending countless dollars and hours on Heroin, not to mention, that as a young man, I had no intention of spending the rest of my days on Earth as a Junkie.  The doctor's words to me were (at 8am), 'By 12pm, you will feel like a Champ!'  I was like sure, whatever...  I was also told that I was only allowed 45mgs to start with.  I didn't like the sound of that.  I told him that I used a lot of Heroin, and that I could handle more.  So, he prescibed me 55mgs, and said that if it wasn't enough, I could ask the next day for an increase (or vice-versa).  He also said that it would take at least an hour and a half for the dose to work.
That was the longest hour and a half ever.  I remember lying in the passenger seat of the car, amidst heavy traffic, waiting for the damn stuff to work.  I was feeling ill at this point....  Suddenly, I felt amazing!  It was like the best feeling in the world.  I came home feeling like a champ!  For the next few weeks, the Methadone acted like a super Heroin high that had no intention of subsiding.  I would wake up and go to sleep that way.  After sometime (a couple months or so), I noticed that I was in need of a higher dose to substain my feeling of 'Normalcy'.  After 6 months, I settled on 120mgs.  A year later (at this present time), I am on 65mgs due to the fact that I am bi-weekly, reducing my dose by 5mgs.  I have aches and pains in all of my joints (worse than arthritis!)...I have stomach problems, fatigue, and mood-swings.  This is a brief description!  If I continued to stay on 120mgs, I would probably feel better, but I have to come to a point where enough is enough.  I continue to reduce my dose...
